rules: All values are synthetic known-answer vectors; this manifest grants no physical qualification.
The declared volume uncertainty bound is a conservative additive bound, not an independence-based root-sum-square estimate.
Source substitution credit is capped by both metered recovered outlet delivery and matched end-use demand.
No source substitution is credited without source identity, current meter calibration, matched use/window and qualified declared-use evidence.
Service floors are hard constraints; no energy or cost benefit compensates for a pressure/flow failure.
Leak metrics are event-level arithmetic and do not establish detector field performance.
Continuity cases are single-use-class inventory/service accounting, not hydraulic, behavioural or optimal-control simulations.
Critical demand is allocated before discretionary demand; discretionary delivery cannot draw below the protected reserve.
Essential service credit requires the stored-water use profile to match the intended-use profile and quality to be admitted.
Source inflow lacking use-specific quality admission is excluded from storage and recorded as rejected inflow.
Outlet capacity is credited only when the service measurement is admitted and the declared pressure/flow floor is met.
South African GN 6292 Regulation 4(1) is represented only as a context-specific >48-hour alternative drinking-water scenario, not as proof of product compliance.
